executionNote.actions: Runs on a GitHub-hosted machine. Free on public repositories, billed per minute on private ones.
executionNote.runners: Runs on one of your enrolled servers through a runner pool. GitHub still schedules it, so a private repository still spends Actions minutes.
executionNote.server: Runs in a container on the Polaris box, without GitHub Actions. Nothing is metered and the repository needs no workflow file.

triggerNote.mention: Somebody names the app in an issue, a pull request or a comment. Always on: it is how people ask for something specific.
triggerNote.issueOpened: A new issue. Useful for triage, or for attempting a fix straight away.
triggerNote.issueLabeled: A label is added to an issue. Pair it with a label so only the ones you mark are picked up.
triggerNote.prOpened: A new pull request, for an automatic review.
triggerNote.prReviewRequested: The app is asked for a review by name.
triggerNote.prReviewSubmitted: Somebody reviewed a pull request, so their feedback can be addressed.
triggerNote.ciFailed: A check run failed, so the logs can be read and a fix attempted.
triggerNote.manual: Started from Polaris, with a prompt you write.

pushPolicyNote.disabled: The agent can read the repository and comment, and cannot push anything.
pushPolicyNote.restricted: The agent can push its own branches and open pull requests. It cannot push to the default branch, delete a branch, or push tags.
pushPolicyNote.enabled: The agent can push anywhere it has access to, including the default branch.

shellPolicyNote.disabled: The agent cannot run commands. It can still read files and use its git and GitHub tools.
shellPolicyNote.restricted: The agent can run commands, with secrets filtered out of the environment they see.
shellPolicyNote.enabled: The agent can run commands with the job's full environment.

gateModeNote.off: The agent pushes as soon as it is done. Its skills and guardrails still apply.
gateModeNote.checks: Runs the commit guard, the convention guardrails and the unfinished-work check before the push. Seconds, no model calls.
gateModeNote.full: Adds the gate's review, test and document passes. Minutes rather than seconds, and the steps are reported on the run.

notice.needsApp: Agents need a GitHub App, which an administrator creates in one click under <link>Integrations</link>. A personal access token is not enough: the agent has to comment and open pull requests as itself.
notice.missingPermission: Runs are paused: the GitHub App is missing a permission that only an administrator can add. Nothing to do here - it starts working again on its own once they have.
notice.notAsked: The GitHub App does not ask for {permissions} yet, so nobody can grant it - there is no request for anyone to accept. GitHub only lets the App's owner change what it asks for, and only by hand.
notice.setOn: Set {permissions} on <link>{url}</link> and save. Each account it is installed on then gets a request to accept, which this screen will ask you for next.
notice.clearsItself: Polaris re-reads what GitHub granted every few minutes, so this clears on its own.
notice.awaitingAdmin: Runs are paused: GitHub is waiting for an administrator to accept a permission request. Nothing to do here - it starts working again on its own once they have.
notice.holding: GitHub is holding a permission request, and until its owner accepts it, runs on these accounts are refused. Only they can accept it - GitHub offers nobody else a way, so this is one of the few things Polaris cannot do for you.
notice.acceptStep: Press Review request, then Accept new permissions.
notice.openOnGithub: Open it under Settings, Applications, on GitHub, then press Review request, then Accept new permissions.
notice.noProvider: No model provider is connected, so a run has nothing to think with. Add one under <link>AI provider keys</link>. The key stays here and is never copied into your repositories.

overview.noRuns: Nothing has run yet. Mention the app in an issue or a pull request, or start a run from a repository.
overview.emptyTitle: No repository has an agent on it yet.
overview.emptyHint: Pick one, choose where its runs should happen, and mention the app in an issue to try it.

page.title: Agents
page.description: Put a coding agent in your repositories. It reviews pull requests, answers issues, fixes failing checks, and opens pull requests when you ask it to.

errors.accessUnchecked: Polaris could not check your GitHub access. Try again in a moment.
errors.unreachableRepo: That repository is not one your GitHub account can reach.
errors.connectProvider: Connect {provider} under Integrations before using this model.
errors.connectProviderDefault: Connect {provider} under Integrations before defaulting to this model.
errors.privateOff: Private repositories are turned off for this account. Change it under Agents settings.
errors.publicOff: Public repositories are turned off for this account. Change it under Agents settings.
errors.notEnabled: That repository is not enabled for agent runs
errors.poolNotYours: That runner pool is not one of yours.

errors.repoNotConnected: That repository is not connected to the Agents app.
errors.noSharedMachine: This Polaris does not offer a shared machine.
errors.serverNotYours: That server is not one of yours.
errors.signInHost: Nothing here signs {agent} in. Either sign it in on that server yourself, or add {ways} under AI keys.
errors.signInLocal: Nothing here signs {agent} in, so it would start and sit at its own login prompt. Add {ways} under AI keys.
errors.taskUnreachable: That task is not one you can reach.
errors.noAnswer: The machine running this session did not answer.

sessions.taskNote: Handed to an agent. It is working on `{branch}` in {repo}: [the session]({href}).
sessions.noneHint: A session puts a coding agent in a branch of its own, on a machine you already have. You can watch it work, answer its questions, and send it the next thing.

form.title: What is it working on
form.noRepo: No repository - just open the agent
form.workspaceHint: It opens on a machine of your own with an empty directory and nothing checked out. The machine keeps its home, so what you install and sign in to stays there for next time.
form.noRepos: Nothing is connected yet. Add one under <link>Repositories</link> to have an agent work in it.
form.command: The command that starts it. It has to already be installed on the machine.
form.sharedOn: One home for the whole deployment: whatever is signed in there signs you in, and the files anybody leaves are the files you find. Sign it in with an API key or a team plan - a personal subscription used by several people is what gets suspended.
form.sharedOff: It opens on a machine of your own, with your logins and your files. Nobody else reaches it.
form.branch: Branch to start from. Leave it empty for the repository's default.
form.prompt: What to start with. Leave it empty to open the agent and type into it yourself.
form.promptPlaceholder: Read the failing test in auth.test.ts and fix what it is telling you.
form.unattendedEnigma: Enigma is on, so this is one of the things it settles: your own policies decide what the agent may run without asking, and Polaris does not add anything on top.
form.unattendedHost: This server is your machine: the agent runs as the account Polaris enrolled, beside everything that account can reach. Off, it asks before each command - which means taking the terminal to answer it.
form.unattendedContainer: It runs in a container of its own holding one checkout, removed when the session ends. Off, it waits on its own permission prompts, and nobody is watching a container.
form.enigmaHint: Installs your policies, conventions and guardrails into the session before the agent starts. Its own settings come from this repository and from Agents settings.

session.installsOnce: The installs happen once. This machine keeps its home, so your next session skips them and starts in seconds.
session.signInHere: If the agent asks you to sign in, do it here. This machine keeps its home between sessions, so it only asks once.
session.nothingSaid: Nothing has been said yet. Whatever you send below goes straight into the agent.
session.noEvents: The agent has not reported anything yet. It reports through its own hooks, which take effect once it has started.
session.ended: This session has ended. Its branch, {branch}, is still there.
session.answerHere: It is waiting on you. Answer it here.

rules.noRepos: Add a repository first. Rules are per repository.
rules.none: No rules yet, so these repositories only answer when the app is mentioned. A rule is what makes one act on its own - reply to a new issue, review a new pull request.
rules.labelsHint: Comma separated. Leave empty for any label.
rules.branchesHint: Comma separated. Leave empty for any branch.
rules.instructionsPlaceholder: Review for correctness and security. Do not comment on formatting.
rules.instructionsHint: Given to the agent alongside what triggered the run. Yours, not the issue author's.

repos.none: No repositories yet. Add one and the agent starts answering when it is mentioned there.
repos.workflowKept: Polaris keeps this workflow file up to date. Open it on GitHub.
repos.workflowMissing: Polaris has not been able to write the workflow file yet.
repos.noProvider: No model provider is connected yet, so runs will fail asking for a key. <link>Add one</link>.
repos.removeBody: The agent stops working there, and its rules and run history go with it. The workflow file, if one was installed, stays in the repository until you delete it.

advice.noPublicAddress: A GitHub-hosted runner has to reach this Polaris instance, and it has no public address yet.
advice.noContainers: This Polaris instance cannot start containers, so it cannot run an agent itself.
advice.noPool: No runner pool covers this repository yet. Add one under Apps > Runners.
advice.public: This repository is public, so GitHub-hosted runners are free and nothing runs on your hardware.
advice.pool: A runner pool already covers this repository, so it runs on your own machine instead of a hosted one.
advice.private: This repository is private, and running it here spends no GitHub Actions minutes.
advice.noAddress: This instance has no public address, so the run happens here rather than on a hosted machine.
advice.hostedPrivate: Nothing here can run it, so it falls to GitHub-hosted runners. A private repository is billed per minute.
advice.hostedFree: GitHub-hosted runners are free for this repository.
advice.nothing: Nothing can run this repository yet. Fix one of the reasons below.

repoDialog.privateOff: Private repositories are turned off for this account. Turn them back on under Agents settings, or the agent will never run here.
repoDialog.publicOff: Public repositories are turned off for this account. Turn them back on under Agents settings, or the agent will never run here.
repoDialog.connectProvider: Connect a model provider under Integrations first.
repoDialog.startsRestricted: The agent starts on feature branches only and cannot push to the default branch. Change that, and the rules that start it, from the repository's settings afterwards.
repoDialog.notCovering: {name} - does not cover this repository yet
repoDialog.widen: Widen that pool's scope to include this repository under Apps > Runners, or its jobs will queue forever.
repoDialog.noPools: You have no runner pools yet. Create one under Apps > Runners, then pick it here.

fix.actions: Give Polaris a public address under Settings > Domains.
fix.runners: Add a pool under Apps > Runners, or point an existing one at this repository.
fix.server: The container engine has to be reachable from Polaris; check Settings > System.

repoDialog.publicShell: This repository is public, so anybody can open a pull request the agent then reads. A full shell hands whatever it runs the provider keys in its environment.

settingsFields.pullRequestsHint: Whether a pull request can start a run. Somebody naming the app in a comment still gets an answer either way.

runs.none: Nothing has run yet. Mention the app in an issue or a pull request, add an automation, or start a run here.
runs.openJob: Open the job that ran this
runs.whatPlaceholder: Add a regression test for the timezone bug in the report exporter, and open a pull request.

settings.allHaveOwn: Every account you have repositories in already has its own settings.

pages.repos: Which repositories the agent works in, and where each one's runs happen. Polaris recommends the cheapest option that fits; the choice is yours.
pages.runs: Every time an agent ran, what started it, and how it ended.
pages.sessions: Agents running right now, in a branch of their own. Watch one, answer it, or send it the next thing.
pages.settings: What your repositories inherit. Set it once here, narrow it per account, and override it on the repositories that need something different.
pages.automations: What starts a run, besides somebody mentioning the app. A repository with no rules still answers a mention.
pages.sessionWorkspace: A workspace of your own, with nothing checked out

setup.description: Three things have to be true before an agent can run. This is where they are.

app.title: Connect a GitHub App
app.body: An App lets the agent comment, review and open pull requests as itself, and lets Polaris hear about issues and pull requests. A personal access token cannot do either. An administrator creates one in a click.

model.title: Connect a model provider
model.body: Your own key with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Groq, Cerebras or OpenRouter, or an OpenAI-compatible gateway. Polaris hands it to a run over an authenticated call and never writes a copy into your repositories, so rotating it takes effect everywhere.

repo.body: Pick where its runs should happen. Polaris recommends the cheapest option that fits: hosted runners for a public repository, your own hardware for a private one.

setup.ready: Everything is in place. Open an issue in one of your repositories and mention {app} to try it.
setup.readyHint: To have it act without being asked, add a rule under Automations.

scopeNotes.all: Skills, the operating contract, the slash commands and the post-edit guardrails.
scopeNotes.policies: The skills and the operating contract. Faster to install, and enough to change how the work is done.

defaultsCard.intro: Anything left on Inherit comes from {from}. A repository can still override any of it.
defaultsCard.pullRequestsHint: Whether a pull request can start a run. A direct mention is answered either way.
defaultsCard.enigmaHint: Installs your policies, conventions and guardrails into every agent before it starts.
defaultsCard.noPools: You have no pools yet. Create one under Apps > Runners.
defaultsCard.fallbackHint: Tried in order when a run is turned away for the account's rate limit, an empty balance, a rejected key, or a window it did not fit in. Drag to reorder.
